title: Holistic Inference Observability Patterns
author: Aisha Raman
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook consolidates patterns we use to observe, profile, benchmark, and operate the Redwood serving runtime end-to-end. It bridges runtime architecture, kernel scheduling signals, profiling playbooks, the benchmarking suite, release-note requirements, common known issues, and short runbooks for on-call responders. The goal is to provide a single, pragmatic reference for engineers instrumenting new routes, kernels, or model variants to ensure consistent SLO alignment and actionable telemetry.

Audience
--------
- Serving runtime engineers
- SREs and capacity planners
- Applied ML and model-onboarding engineers
- Devs instrumenting SDKs and SDK-facing endpoints

Design principles
-----------------
- Observability must answer the three questions: What happened? Why did it happen? What should I do next?
- Prioritize pay-for-value telemetry: high-cardinality traces for failures, aggregated metrics for trends.
- Instrument along the request path boundaries: ingress, routing/decision, kernel scheduling, kvcache, hw-dispatch, egress.
- Telemetry must be actionable within 2 minutes (alerts) and diagnostic within 30 minutes (traces + flamegraphs).

Key services and signal owners
-----------------------------
- runtime-gateway (owner: runtime-api) — ingress latencies, auth errors
- dispatchd (owner: kernel-scheduler) — kernel queue lengths, slot utilization, preemptions
- kvcache-service (owner: kvcache) — hit/miss, warmup rate, eviction pressure
- runtime-exec (owner: runtime-core) — per-kernel exec time, memory high-water marks
- telemetry-ingest (owner: observability) — sampling, event drop rate, pipeline lag

Minimum SLOs and alert thresholds
---------------------------------
- Short-response generation (<= 128 tokens): p95 latency < 130ms, p99 < 250ms.
- Long-response generation (>= 512 tokens): p95 latency < 1200ms, p99 < 2200ms.
- Kernel queue depth: alert when avg queue depth > 80% of capacity for 5 minutes.
- kvcache hit rate: warn when hot-prefix hit-rate drops > 10% vs baseline.
- Telemetry ingestion lag: page when pipeline lag > 2 minutes for 5m window.

Observability patterns (practical)
--------------------------------
1) Transactional tracing per request
   - Propagate a single trace_id across components: runtime-gateway -> routing -> dispatchd -> kernel -> telemetry-ingest.
   - Use tags: model.name, model.variant, sequence_length_bucket, customer_tier, kernel_hint, gpu_type.
   - Attach sampling hint: sample on errors and on tail latencies (p99 triggers).

2) Two-tier metrics approach
   - Aggregated metrics (prometheus): qps, token/s, p50/p95/p99 latencies, kernel_slot_occupancy, kvcache_hit_rate.
   - High-cardinality logs and traces: request payload hashes, input signature, failure stack.

3) Kernel-level observability
   - Expose per-kernel metrics: kernel.exec_ms, kernel.wait_ms, kernel.preempt_count, kernel.context_switches.
   - Maintain a kernel-health triple: (avg_exec_ms, exec_variance_ms, preempt_rate).

4) Workload-aware sampling
   - Always sample 100% of 5xx errors and any request with kernel.exec_ms > p99_threshold.
   - Use probabilistic sampling by customer_tier: 0.5% for free, 5% for standard, 25% for enterprise.

Telemetry schema (table)
-----------------------
Metric name | Type | Retention | Notes
----------- | ---- | --------- | -----
request.latency_ms | histogram | 90d | label: model, variant, route
kernel.exec_ms | histogram | 30d | label: kernel_name, gpu_family, shard_id
kvcache.hit_rate | gauge | 180d | 1m and 1h resolutions
telemetry.pipeline_lag_ms | gauge | 30d | alerts when > 120000 ms
dispatchd.queue_depth | gauge | 14d | per-pool view

Example trace span model (text)
-------------------------------
- span: ingress.request (service=runtime-gateway)
  - tags: {trace_id, request_id, model.name, client_id}
- span: route.evaluate (service=routing)
  - tags: {routing_policy, fallback_used}
- span: kernel.schedule (service=dispatchd)
  - tags: {kernel_hint, slot_id, scheduled_delay_ms}
- span: kernel.exec (service=runtime-exec)
  - logs: {flamegraph_blob_id}

Profiling playbook (step-by-step)
--------------------------------
1) Pre-checks before profiling
   - Confirm test harness: bench-client v2.3.1 and that model/version pinned.
   - Ensure telemetry-ingest is sampling errors at 100% and enabled for p99 tail traces.
2) Reproduce or collect baseline
   - Run synthetic workload: bench-client --profile-shape mixed_short_long --duration 15m --concurrency 64
   - Record p50/p95/p99, token/s, kernel.exec_ms distributions. Save baseline id.
3) Controlled sampling & flamegraph capture
   - Flip kernel debug flag: dispatchd/admin api PATCH /debug/kernel-trace?duration=60s&sample_rate=1.0
   - Collect flamegraph blob from runtime-exec: curl -s http://runtime-exec:8080/debug/flame?id=<blob_id> > flame.svg
4) Diagnose
   - Compare kernel.wait_ms vs exec_ms: if wait_ms >> exec_ms, focus on scheduling and preemption.
   - Use trace waterfall to find serialization points (eg. bottleneck at kvcache warmup).
5) Mitigate and verify
   - Small mitigations: increase dispatchd slot_count by 15% for the affected pool, enable prefix caching for hot routes.
   - Re-run bench-client for 10m and compare to baseline.

Benchmarking suite integration notes
----------------------------------
- Add new kernel variants to the regression suite by creating a descriptor under /bench/descriptors with fields: name, model_compat, input_shape_samples, expected_p99.
- Bench script example: ./bench/runner --descriptor small-llama-13b-quant --iterations 500 --report-to bench-results/serviceX/2026-02-01
- Bench result table (example)

Model Variant | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | tokens/s | notes
------------- | -------: | ------: | -----: | -------: | -----
llama-13b-8bit-quant | 42 | 110 | 210 | 480 | tuned-kernel-v2
llama-13b-bf16 | 55 | 140 | 320 | 420 | high-precision path

Release notes checklist (for runtime releases)
---------------------------------------------
- Document kernel changes and expected perf delta (p50/p95/p99) per variant.
- List config toggles with safe defaults and rollout plan (canary matrix).
- Add required telemetry fields and their schema versions.
- Add a smoke-runbook with exact bench commands and thresholds.

Known issues and mitigations (operational)
----------------------------------------
1) Symptom: sudden p99 spike for short-response routes
   - Likely causes: kernel preemption, kvcache cold miss, network tail on telemetry-ingest.
   - Quick checks: `kubectl top pods -n runtime | grep dispatchd` ; check dispatchd.queue_depth > 0 ; check kvcache hit rate.
   - Mitigation: increase dispatchd slots for pool, temporarily enable kvcache-prefetch for hot-prefix, lift per-tenant concurrency cap.
2) Symptom: dispatchd OOM during heavy mixed workloads
   - Cause: kernel slot memory accounting drift after recent kernel-change.
   - Mitigation: drain node, restart dispatchd, roll back kernel commit, open PR to add stronger accounting and unit tests.

Operational runbooks (quick actions)
----------------------------------
- Runbook: tail-latency spike
  1. Pager triggers alert: p99 latency > configured threshold.
  2. On-call: query `prometheus` for kernel.exec_ms distribution and `dispatchd.queue_depth`.
  3. If queue_depth is high, increase slot_scale for the affected pool (dispatchd/admin scale).
  4. If preempt_rate increased, roll back recent kernel rollout in the canary matrix.
  5. If kvcache hit-rate dropped, trigger kvcache warmup script: `tools/warmup-prefixes --prefix-file /tmp/hot-prefixes.csv`

- Runbook: telemetry pipeline lag
  1. Check telemetry-ingest pods and SQS/Kafka backlog.
  2. If backlog present, temporarily reduce sampling rate for standard/free tiers via admin API.
  3. If ingestion still behind, admit reduced retention for metrics to reduce ingestion pressure.

Appendix: example telemetry event (JSON)
--------------------------------------
{
  "trace_id": "9f1d3a2b4c",
  "request_id": "r-123456",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-14T15:04:22Z",
  "model": "llama-13b-8bit-quant",
  "variant": "tuned-kernel-v2",
  "metrics": {
    "request.latency_ms": 218,
    "kernel.exec_ms": 182,
    "kvcache.hit": false
  },
  "tags": ["enterprise", "route:chat"]
}

Appendix: common CLI/debug commands
-----------------------------------
- Check node-level GPU utilization: `kubectl top nodes --selector=gpu=true --containers`
- Check dispatchd queue: `http :8080/dispatchd/metrics | jq .queue_depth`
- Fetch flamegraph: `curl http://runtime-exec:8080/debug/flame?id=<blob_id> -o flame.svg`
- Run benchmark: `bench-client --descriptor small-llama-13b-quant --concurrency 32 --duration 600`

Notes and next steps
--------------------
- We will iterate on the schema versioning strategy for telemetry (v1 -> v2) to make kernel tags backwards compatible.
- Short-term roadmap items: enrich kernel spans with GPU SM occupancy, add cross-tenant memory eviction metrics, and automate warmup for top-100 hot prefixes.

If you are adding new instrumentation or a kernel variant, follow the checklist in "Release notes checklist" and file a PR that includes updated telemetry schema and a bench descriptor. For questions, ping #runtime-observability on Slack or assign to the owner team (observability).
